The only theorem about Nat.nextPowerOfTwo is Nat.isPowerOfTwo_nextPowerOfTwo.

I found myself needing n ≤ Nat.nextPowerOfTwo n and n ≤ 2 ^ j → Nat.nextPowerOfTwo n ≤ 2 ^ j. However, i struggled a lot trying to prove them since I couldn't unfold the definition somehow... Then I asked Aristotle to do it and it came up with an abomination that uses metaprogramming to achieve this very unfolding (e.g., the file fails if imports are replaced using #min_imports).

How would one prove these theorems without metaprogramming? Is it easy enough that we don't need them in Mathlib? (I assume the bar for adding theorems directly to lean4 is higher than for Mathlib?)

import Mathlib

/-! # Lemmas about `Nat.nextPowerOfTwo`

Since `Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.go` is private, we create an alias and its equation lemma
via metaprogramming to reason about the internal loop directly,
-/

open Lean Elab Command Meta in
run_cmd do
  let base : Name := Name.anonymous.str "_private" |>.str "Init" |>.str "Data"
    |>.str "Nat" |>.str "Power2" |>.str "Basic" |>.num 0 |>.str "Nat"
    |>.str "nextPowerOfTwo"
  let goName := base.str "go"
  let eqDefName := goName.str "eq_def"
  let env ← getEnv
  let some goInfo := env.find? goName | throwError "go not found"
  liftCoreM <| addDecl <| Declaration.defnDecl {
    name := `Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.goAlias
    levelParams := goInfo.levelParams
    type := goInfo.type
    value := mkConst goName (goInfo.levelParams.map Level.param)
    hints := .regular 0
    safety := .safe
  }
  let some eqInfo := env.find? eqDefName | throwError "eq_def not found"
  liftCoreM <| addDecl <| Declaration.thmDecl {
    name := `Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.goAlias_eq_def
    levelParams := eqInfo.levelParams
    type := eqInfo.type
    value := mkConst eqDefName (eqInfo.levelParams.map Level.param)
  }

private lemma goAlias_unfold (n power : ℕ) (h : power > 0) :
    Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.goAlias n power h =
      if power < n then Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.goAlias n (power * 2) (by positivity)
      else power :=
  Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.goAlias_eq_def n power h

private lemma goAlias_ge (n power : ℕ) (h : power > 0) :
    n ≤ Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.goAlias n power h := by
  rw [goAlias_unfold]
  split
  · exact goAlias_ge n (power * 2) (by positivity)
  · omega
termination_by n - power
decreasing_by omega

private lemma goAlias_le (n power : ℕ) (h : power > 0) (j : ℕ)
    (hn : n ≤ 2 ^ j) (hp : power ≤ 2 ^ j) (hpow : power.isPowerOfTwo) :
    Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.goAlias n power h ≤ 2 ^ j := by
  rw [goAlias_unfold]
  split
  · rename_i hlt
    obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hpow
    have hkj : k < j := by
      by_contra hc
      push Not at hc
      exact not_lt.mpr (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) hc) (lt_of_lt_of_le hlt hn)
    have hpow2 : 2 ^ k * 2 = 2 ^ (k + 1) := by ring
    have hle : 2 ^ (k + 1) ≤ 2 ^ j := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
    exact goAlias_le n (2 ^ k * 2) (by positivity) j hn
      (hpow2 ▸ hle) (Nat.isPowerOfTwo_mul_two_of_isPowerOfTwo ⟨k, rfl⟩)
  · exact hp
termination_by n - power
decreasing_by omega

lemma nextPow2_nat_ge (n : ℕ) : n ≤ Nat.nextPowerOfTwo n :=
  goAlias_ge n 1 (by omega)

lemma nextPow2_nat_le (n j : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 2 ^ j) : Nat.nextPowerOfTwo n ≤ 2 ^ j :=
  goAlias_le n 1 (by omega) j hn (Nat.one_le_pow j 2 (by omega)) Nat.isPowerOfTwo_one

module
import Mathlib
import all Init.Data.Nat.Power2.Basic

/-! # Lemmas about `Nat.nextPowerOfTwo` -/

private lemma go_ge (n power : ℕ) (h : power > 0) :
    n ≤ Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.go n power h := by
  rw [Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.go]
  split
  · exact go_ge n (power * 2) (by positivity)
  · omega
termination_by n - power
decreasing_by omega

private lemma go_le (n power : ℕ) (h : power > 0) (j : ℕ)
    (hn : n ≤ 2 ^ j) (hp : power ≤ 2 ^ j) (hpow : power.isPowerOfTwo) :
    Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.go n power h ≤ 2 ^ j := by
  rw [Nat.nextPowerOfTwo.go]
  split
  · rename_i hlt
    obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hpow
    have hkj : k < j := by
      by_contra hc
      push Not at hc
      exact not_lt.mpr (Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) hc) (lt_of_lt_of_le hlt hn)
    have hpow2 : 2 ^ k * 2 = 2 ^ (k + 1) := by ring
    have hle : 2 ^ (k + 1) ≤ 2 ^ j := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by omega) (by omega)
    exact go_le n (2 ^ k * 2) (by positivity) j hn
      (hpow2 ▸ hle) (Nat.isPowerOfTwo_mul_two_of_isPowerOfTwo ⟨k, rfl⟩)
  · exact hp
termination_by n - power
decreasing_by omega

lemma nextPow2_nat_ge (n : ℕ) : n ≤ Nat.nextPowerOfTwo n :=
  go_ge n 1 (by omega)

lemma nextPow2_nat_le (n j : ℕ) (hn : n ≤ 2 ^ j) : Nat.nextPowerOfTwo n ≤ 2 ^ j :=
  go_le n 1 (by omega) j hn (Nat.one_le_pow j 2 (by omega)) Nat.isPowerOfTwo_one

I guess it's really time to learn about the module system and start using it... Thanks!
Do you think it makes sense to add those lemmas to Mathlib?
I think the lemma you really want is Nat.nextPowerOfTwo = 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 n
That saves you having to create any interesting API for nextPowerOfTwo

Using the previous two lemmas,

lemma nextPowerOfTwo_eq_two_pow_clog (n : ℕ) : n.nextPowerOfTwo = 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 n := by
  have hle := nextPow2_nat_ge n
  obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := Nat.isPowerOfTwo_nextPowerOfTwo n
  rw [hk]
  simp_all only [Order.lt_two_iff, zero_le, ne_eq, OfNat.ofNat_ne_one, not_false_eq_true, pow_right_inj₀]
  apply_fun Nat.clog 2 at hle using Nat.clog_monotone 2
  have clogpow (k : ℕ) : Nat.clog 2 (2 ^ k) = k := by simp_all only [Order.lt_two_iff, le_refl, Nat.clog_pow]
  rw [clogpow] at hle
  suffices k ≤ Nat.clog 2 n by linarith
  have : n.nextPowerOfTwo ≤ 2 ^ Nat.clog 2 n :=
    (nextPow2_nat_le n <| Nat.clog 2 n) <| Nat.le_pow_clog (by decide) n
  rw [hk] at this
  apply_fun Nat.clog 2 at this using Nat.clog_monotone 2
  simpa [clogpow] using this

(I guess an AI would write a better proof at this point and this was just an exercise which took me embarrassingly long for an ugly proof)
